**Temporal focus:**
T1. Historical observation — YES
T2. Forward-looking immediate — YES
T3. Long-term development — YES

**Synopsis:**
US Treasury Secretary Bessent, on the sidelines of a G20 finance leaders' meeting, publicly pressured Japan to accelerate BOJ rate hikes and abandon Abenomics-era expansionary fiscal policy. One month after a rare joint USD/JPY intervention, Bessent signaled no appetite for repeat FX support, effectively locking the BOJ into a September rate hike and pushing for a faster hiking cycle. He also warned against excessive fiscal spending under PM Takaichi, whose ambitious budget plans have driven JGB yields to 30-year highs — a dynamic with direct spillover risk to US Treasury yields. Oxford Economics now projects BOJ hikes in Sep/Dec 2026 and Apr 2027.

---

**Q01. Relevance to US economy, US yields, US interest rates, US market pricing?**
Relevance: IMPLICIT
*(JGB yield surges at 30-year highs carry explicit spillover risk to US Treasury yields; yen dynamics affect global risk positioning and USD flows — highly relevant to US rates markets even if not the primary focus)*

Increasing rates magnitude: ~0.50–0.75% cumulative BOJ hikes implied over 2026–2027 (3 hikes at ~25bp each)
Increasing rates short-term: YES *(Sep + Dec 2026 hikes expected)*
Increasing rates long-term: YES *(Apr 2027 and implied further trajectory)*

**Q03. Rate increase expectancy score:**
Expectancy score: **25/100**
*(Sep hike was already widely priced; the incremental news is the US pressure accelerating the pace and the Dec 2026 / Apr 2027 additions — partially new but not a full surprise)*
